newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures in late sell-off on NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures in late sell-off on NY.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures ended Wednesday broadly mixed, with nearby months posting heavy losses in a late sell-off on sharp falls in New York.
Traders said the market was earlier supported by short-covering against July by one major European trade house.
But towards the London close, New York arabica increased losses amid forecasts of a warm, sub-tropical ridge of high pressure building in Brazil coffee belt.
June and July are the frost danger months but so far this month, temperatures have been above freezing point.
July finished $60 down at $1,840 per tonne while benchmark September stood $45 lower at $1,865. September's resistance was pegged at $2,000, followed by a heavy barrier at $2,065.
July/September and September/November switches again accounted for the bulk of the volume, which reached 7,486 lots by the close.
The July/September spread, which narrowed to $4 at one stage, widened again to end Wednesday at $25.
Both London and New York rebounded on Tuesday in reaction to an oversold situation following the release of what many had described as bearish U.S. Department of Agriculture coffee estimates.
But the prices came back on somewhat bullish U.S. consumer coffee stocks data and the fall in U.S. certified stocks.
